Fewer stations, up to €19 a kilo and bets that are narrowing

Up to €19 a kilo in Germany

00Summary

Hydrogen in transport is narrowing

In 2026 hydrogen in transport is narrowing: it grows in two markets and in the brands that keep betting on it, while the station network shrinks in Germany and Japan and the kilo reaches €19 in Germany.

Sales of fuel cell cars rose in 2025 to 16,011 units, 24.4% more than in 2024, but according to SNE Research every market outside China and South Korea fell. In the first half of 2026, 4,643 were sold, 13% more than a year earlier, with Hyundai at 3,337 (+161.9%) and Toyota at 306 (-56.7%).

The network is shrinking in Germany and Japan. Germany has about 50 public stations open in January 2026, against more than 80 two years earlier. Japan counts 149. In California, 50 are open and 11 are out of service, with average availability close to 60%. Refuelling costs up to about €19 a kilo in Germany.

GM and its joint venture with Honda are leaving, and the projects with public money remain. GM ended development of next-generation fuel cells and its joint venture with Honda will stop producing before the end of 2026; Arthur Bus and Quantron went insolvent. Hyundai, BMW and Toyota carry on, along with the European truck alliance, €220m of German aid and the European Hydrogen Bank, while Daimler's series production of trucks is postponed from 2027 to the 2030s.

From the analysis
Before you read

How to read the figures

Scope: hydrogen as a fuel for road vehicles (cars, trucks and buses) and their refuelling stations. Hydrogen production appears only where it affects transport: public aid and manufacturers' electrolysers. Ships, trains, aviation, industry and stationary hydrogen are out of scope.

Marks: every figure's source is listed with its URL at the end of the page. “Own calculation” marks arithmetic on figures that already carry a source.

Selection rule: a figure or fact is included only if the cited page was read. Nothing is estimated. "ND" means there is no defensible figure.

Two caveats apply throughout: figures for different countries have different dates and definitions and are not added up; and a plan or a target is not a fact.

01Cars

Cars: growth in just two markets

16,011 fuel cell cars were sold worldwide in 2025, 24.4% more than in 2024. By market: China 7,797 (the source calls the figure "commercial"), South Korea 6,802, Europe 566, Japan 430 and North America 365. According to the same source, every market outside China and South Korea fell.

By brand, Hyundai sold 6,861 (+78.9%, with the second-generation Nexo) and Toyota 1,168 (-39.1%). In Japan, Nikkei counts 431 sales in 2025, 83% fewer than in 2021.

In the first half of 2026, 4,643 units were sold worldwide against 4,110 a year earlier (+13%). Hyundai sold 3,337 (+161.9%), Toyota 306 (-56.7%) and Chinese commercial vehicles 921 (-54.4%).

The new Nexo costs from €69,900 in Germany (the previous one, from €77,290), with 826 km of range and a hydrogen consumption of 0.8 to 0.9 kg per 100 km. BMW will launch the iX5 Hydrogen in 2028, with €273m of public aid from the federal government and Bavaria; the 750 km range is a target.

02Stations

Stations: few and concentrated

Interact Analysis counted 1,369 hydrogen stations deployed worldwide at the end of 2024: 849 in Asia-Pacific (62%), 412 in Europe, the Middle East and Africa and 108 in the Americas. China, South Korea, Japan, France and Germany account for 79%. It is a single-source count: there is no worldwide count for 2026.

The 2026 country figures show a network that is shrinking or not taking off:

  • Germany: about 50 public stations open in January 2026 (13 with 700 bar only, 35 with both pressures and 2 with 350 bar only); two years earlier there were more than 80.
  • Japan: 149 stations in February 2026, 10% fewer than five years ago and less than half the 320 the government had planned.
  • California: 50 stations open to the public on 2 September 2025 and 11 temporarily out of service. Average network availability over the last year was close to 60%. There are 14,128 fuel cell cars registered (April 2025).
  • China: 574 stations and more than 360 t/day of capacity at the end of 2025; an official cited more than 590 in June 2026.

Element 2, which was building stations in the United Kingdom, had a winding-up petition served in September 2026; the article does not confirm the liquidation.

03Price

What a kilo costs

In Germany hydrogen costs up to about €19/kg at the pump (gross price, January 2026); prices are dynamic and vary by region and pressure. H2 Mobility has cut the price by about 10% at 5 stations (1 June) and by 12 to 16% at 15 stations (1 October); none of the sources read gives the absolute price before and after. For trucks, the hylane tariff at H2 Mobility stations is about €8/kg net from 1 January 2026, only with its card and for contracted volumes.

Own calculation: with a consumption of 0.8 to 0.9 kg per 100 km and the maximum price of €19/kg, a car spends €15 to 17 on hydrogen per 100 km. It is a ceiling: at stations with a price cut it would be somewhat less. There is no verified electricity price, so it is not compared with a battery-electric car.

In China the kilo costs 35 to 76 yuan in the pilot cities and the target of three ministries is to get below 25 yuan in 2030. It is not converted to euros.

The US Department of Energy's goals (May 2024 plan) are USD 2/kg for production in 2026 and USD 1/kg in 2031, USD 7/kg for hydrogen dispensed to heavy-duty vehicles in 2028 and USD 80/kW for the heavy-transport fuel cell system in 2030. They are goals, not actual costs; the DOE site warns that a new plan is coming.

04Trucks

Trucks: series production slips, pilots continue

Daimler Truck says its customers have driven almost 600,000 km with fuel cell trucks and plans to deploy a small series of 100 next-generation fuel cell trucks with customers from the end of 2026. It is a plan, not deliveries. electrive recalls that Daimler delayed series production from 2027 to the 2030s.

On 15 September 2026 Daimler, Volvo, Toyota, Bosch, Air Liquide, TotalEnergies, TEAL Mobility and MB Energy announced cooperation on hydrogen mobility in Europe, with a horizon of 2030. Daimler is also preparing hydrogen combustion engine trucks, which according to the release would come out "next year".

The Rhenus pilot with Daimler GenH2 trucks on liquid hydrogen measures a consumption of 5.6 to 8.0 kg per 100 km and adds up to about 225,000 km in phase 1 (5 trucks). Phase 2 has five customers. According to the source, there are only two liquid hydrogen stations in Germany.

The German government has put €220m of aid into the hydrogen truck network; more than 70 stations and 800 trucks were applied for, with more than 500 applications in the first call, which would be decided in the second half of 2026. Thailand approved 1,490 million baht (about €39m) to produce the Toyota Hilux FCEV from December 2027, up to 3,000 units a year.

Quantron became insolvent at the end of October 2024, its founder bought the assets on 1 April 2025 and in September 2026 Quantron and HyperView set up a joint venture in China, with Foxconn as manufacturer. It expects 100 pre-series vehicles at the end of 2026: this is a plan.

05Buses

Buses: small fleets

The US Fuel Cell and Hydrogen Energy Association (FCHEA, an industry source) reports small and growing fleets: SamTrans has 10 buses in service and 108 more approved; Victor Valley presented 13 earlier in 2026; Montebello put 3 into operation in August 2026; New York's MTA received 2 in June 2026 and its future Gun Hill station could serve 40; Rochester RTS has 2 and will acquire 10 more. Three New York agencies receive USD 52.5m from the Zero-Emission Transit Transition programme (October 2025). The source itself says operation is concentrated in pilots and relatively small fleets.

In Europe, Arthur Bus (Poland) filed for insolvency on 26 November 2025, affecting 20 buses ordered by Lublin and 3 by Buspunkt.

06Exits and bets

Who leaves and who bets

Exits and insolvencies. In October 2025 GM ended development of next-generation fuel cells and cancelled a USD 55m plant in Detroit; it had invested almost USD 3,000m since the late nineties. Its joint venture with Honda (FCSM) will stop producing before the end of 2026. To these are added Arthur Bus, Quantron and Element 2.

Bets and aid. In November 2026 Hyundai unveiled its first 5 MW PEM electrolyser, with series production in 2027, and signed a non-binding agreement with Air Liquide on hydrogen mobility in China. In the third auction the European Hydrogen Bank signed €62m for Gen2 Energy (Norway, €3.48/kg for ten years) and €139.8m for Hy2gen (Denmark, €0.97/kg for ten years).

07China

China: target and reality

China's target is 100,000 fuel cell vehicles in 2030; the five pilot city clusters had sold 39,023. In the first half of 2026 sales were 550 according to CAAM (-63.5%) and 921 commercial vehicles according to SNE Research (-54.4%): they use different definitions. In the fourth quarter of 2025 more than 3,000 units a month were exceeded.

08Who is who

Who is who, as of 18 November 2026

Daimler Truck

Almost 600,000 km with customers' fuel cell trucks; plan for 100 new trucks from the end of 2026; series production delayed from 2027 to the 2030s (according to electrive).

Toyota

1,168 fuel cell cars sold in 2025 (-39.1%); Hilux FCEV in Thailand from December 2027; member of the European truck alliance.

Hyundai

6,861 fuel cell cars sold in 2025 (+78.9%); new Nexo from €69,900 in Germany; 5 MW electrolyser; non-binding agreement with Air Liquide in China.

General Motors and Honda

GM ended development of next-generation fuel cells (October 2025); its joint venture with Honda will stop producing before the end of 2026.

BMW

iX5 Hydrogen for 2028, with €273m of public aid.

Air Liquide

50% co-owner of TEAL Mobility with TotalEnergies; member of the European truck alliance; non-binding agreement with Hyundai.

Volvo, Bosch, TotalEnergies and MB Energy

Members of the European hydrogen truck alliance of September 2026.

H2 Mobility (Germany)

Price cuts: about 10% at 5 stations (1 June 2026) and 12 to 16% at 15 stations (1 October).

Rhenus

Pilot with a Daimler Truck GenH2 truck on liquid hydrogen: 5.6 to 8.0 kg/100 km.

Quantron

Insolvent in 2024; assets bought by its founder in April 2025; joint venture with HyperView in China in September 2026.

Arthur Bus

Filed for insolvency on 26 November 2025.

Element 2

Winding-up petition served in September 2026; the liquidation is not confirmed.

09What to watch

What to watch

  1. From the end of 2026
    Daimler: 100 next-generation trucks with customers

    It is the first series of the new generation and series production was already postponed to the 2030s.

  2. Before the end of 2026
    End of the Honda and GM fuel cell joint venture

    Honda continues on its own; GM has already left development.

  3. Second half of 2026
    Germany: decision on aid to the truck network

    More than 70 stations and 800 trucks were applied for against €220m of aid.

  4. After November 2026
    European Hydrogen Bank: rest of the third auction

    More than €1,000m in total is expected; the first two signed awards are €62m and €139.8m.

  5. 2027
    Hyundai: series production of electrolysers

    Hyundai presents its first own electrolyser and is building a fuel cell stack plant in Ulsan for 30,000 a year.

  6. 2028
    Toyota Hilux FCEV and BMW iX5 Hydrogen

    BMW has €273m of public aid and Thailand approved the Hilux investment.

  7. 2030
    China: targets of 100,000 vehicles and under 25 yuan/kg

    Today there are 39,023 vehicles in the pilot clusters and the kilo costs 35 to 76 yuan.
